title: Upper Savannah utility watershed source context

utilities.title: ARJWS — Six and Twenty focus watersheds

reference.basis: The issuer appendix identifies Upper Six and Twenty Creek and Lower Six and Twenty Creek as ARJWS focus watersheds. The selected whole HUC12 units anchor contributing-land planning.

utilities.title: PRWD — Tugaloo and Choestoea focus watersheds

reference.basis: The issuer appendix identifies Choestoea Creek and Lower Tugaloo River as PRWD focus watersheds. The selected whole HUC12 units anchor contributing-land planning.

interpretation.geography: Whole HUC12 planning footprints follow retained ToHUC links to the issuer-selected anchors. Published intake protection polygons retain a separate source and geometry.
interpretation.areas: USGS whole-HUC fields, NRCS whole-HUC acres and NRCS state-portion acres preserve their original editions and rounding. Each HUC is counted once in a union; state rows are summed once per state/HUC.
interpretation.nrcs: FY26 priority is a state-specific programme designation. Ground, Surface and Both are retained separately; a Ground designation is not a surface-intake water-quality measurement or an NDR subsurface parameter.
interpretation.classifications: Selected South Carolina class counts follow the publisher HUC_12 attribute. Zero target records does not classify an entire watershed's waters. Georgia and North Carolina designation coverage is outside this source's jurisdiction.
interpretation.native_models: InVEST 3.20 NDR/SDR estimate land-origin export reaching the modeled stream network. HUC relationships associate that land with the selected receptor. In-stream retention, reservoir processes and intake concentrations require additional modeling.

native_units.retained_cell_mass: Native rate multiplied by original native cell area in hectares once
native_units.reported_polygon_total: Retained cell mass multiplied by its selected reporting overlap fraction, then summed
native_units.paired_change: Alternative minus baseline on common finite support; reduction is the negative of that change
